name: Serpentine Belt
summary: Upgraded from BLOCKED. The BMW ETK diagram 'Belt drive - generator/AC/power steering' (RealOEM decode of this VIN's tail: E90 LCI 328i sedan, N52N, built 09/2009, US) settles the part-number conflicts: ribbed V-belt 6PK1990 = 11287628650 (older numbers 11287549150/11287527564 are previous revisions per Turner), mechanical belt tensioner = 11288624196 with M11x65 ALUMINIUM Torx screw 11287530315 ('aluminium screws may only be used once'), deflection pulley 11287535860, protective caps 11287535867 and 11281435114. Engine is N52N per ETK; the same belt number is listed by a retailer for N51, N52N and N53 so N51-vs-N52 no longer matters for the belt. Two independent secondary procedures (FCP Euro N52 article; Pelican Parts E90 article) agree on T60 tensioner release rotating clockwise and removing intake ducting/airbox (and fan shroud on one) first. Tensioner bolt torque 25 Nm + 90 degrees is corroborated by FCP plus four forum sources but NO BMW document (VERIFIED_SECONDARY, primary:false). Idler (deflection) pulley bolt torque is CONFLICT (40 Nm vs 80 Nm) and must not be published. Still missing: lock-pin diameter, a belt routing diagram, alternator pulley torque, the official BMW repair instruction. Publish with VERIFIED_SECONDARY labels and a torque-specs caveat, or hold the idler torque back.
variantDependencies: Engine: ETK decode of the VIN tail = N52N (US 328i). A retailer lists the same 6PK1990 belt 11287628650 for 328i N51, 323i/325i/330i N52/N52N and N53, so the belt number is not engine-split on E90 LCI.
Transmission: automatic cars have one extra T25 fastener (transmission oil cooler on the fan shroud) in the FCP procedure; this car's transmission is unknown.

Belt carries alternator, power steering pump and A/C compressor on one belt with one tensioner (Turner, BimmerWorld, ETK diagram title). Turner notes exclusions only for X5 with Adaptive Drive/4-zone climate; no E90 option split found in ETK.
Alternator pulley removal may need a special tool (BimmerWorld CTA-8088 for Bosch alternators); only if the alternator pulley itself is being replaced.

Access path differs by source: FCP removes airbox and fan shroud; Pelican removes the front intake duct, a duct across the radiator and a 6 mm Allen fastener and raises the front of the car; E60 poster removed the fan shroud to get tool clearance.

tools.item: T60 Torx socket/bit on a long-handled ratchet or breaker bar (tensioner release)
tools.note: Two independent step-by-step articles; also a 5series poster mentions a large Torx/T50 uncertainly. Schwaben N54 tool uses T60 head.

tools.note: FCP says to pull the lock pin after routing the belt (implies the new tensioner carries a pin); Pelican staff say no pin is needed. Pin diameter not given anywhere.

steps.title: Prepare
steps.instruction: Work on a cool engine with the key out. Note that the aluminium tensioner bolt is single-use and the tensioner spring is strong.
warnings: Keep hands, hair and clothing clear of belt and fan.
Tensioner is under considerable spring force; do not release it uncontrolled.

steps.title: Clear access to the belt
steps.instruction: Remove the air intake snorkel/duct and airbox (FCP: snorkel two fasteners, airbox two 10 mm bolts, hose clamp, MAF connector). Pelican alternative: two T20 at the front duct, loosen clamp and turn the hose lock 90 degrees, remove the 6 mm Allen fastener and raise the front. Remove the fan assembly if you need room for the tool (FCP: unplug the connector, free the expansion tank line, T25 at the shroud top; automatics also have a T25 oil-cooler fastener).
warnings: Unplug the MAF sensor cleanly; do not strain connectors.
Fan shroud fits tightly; wiggle it clear.
steps.sourcesNote: Both approaches documented; which is needed depends on tool and fan clearance.

steps.title: Record belt path
steps.instruction: Photograph or sketch the belt path and note direction of rotation before removing anything. The order given is crank, A/C compressor, power steering pump, idler, alternator, tensioner; no official diagram was found.
warnings: If photos and the new belt do not match, stop; routing differs by model per Pelican staff.

steps.title: Release the tensioner and take the belt off
steps.instruction: Fit a T60 on a long-handled ratchet in the tensioner release point, rotate clockwise and hold, lift the belt off the tensioner pulley, then off the other pulleys.
warnings: Release slowly; keep fingers out of the belt path; a slipping bit can injure.
Do not use an undersized tool.

steps.title: Inspect
steps.instruction: Fold the belt to check rib cracks, glazing and chunks; spin the idler and tensioner pulleys for play, rough rotation or noise; replace worn parts. Replace tensioner and idler together with the belt when they are worn (kit recommended).

steps.title: Replace the idler pulley (optional)
steps.instruction: Pry off the idler caps with a flat screwdriver, remove the 16 mm deep-socket bolt that holds the pulley to the alternator, fit the new pulley by hand to avoid cross-threading, reinstall caps. Torque is NOT publishable (40 Nm vs 80 Nm conflict).
warnings: Do not guess the torque; use BMW repair data.

steps.title: Replace the tensioner (optional)
steps.instruction: Remove the single E14 mounting bolt and the tensioner. Fit the new tensioner with a NEW single-use aluminium M11x65 bolt: thread by hand, torque 25 Nm then a further 90 degrees. Remove any retaining disc on the back of the new pulley if the kit instructs (E82 post).
warnings: Aluminium bolt may only be used once (BMW ETK).
Never reuse the bolt; torque + angle figure is from secondary sources, not a BMW document.

steps.title: Route the new belt
steps.instruction: Use the 6PK1990 belt 11287628650. Seat it on the crank pulley first (slide in sideways), then A/C compressor, power steering pump, idler and alternator, and finally onto the tensioner pulley while the T60 holds tension released. Check every rib is in its groove.
warnings: A mis-seated belt can jump off or shred.

steps.title: Apply tension
steps.instruction: Let the tensioner back slowly; if a lock pin is fitted, pull it out only after the belt is correctly routed (FCP). Re-check seating.
warnings: Pin size and location not documented; Pelican says no pin is used.

steps.title: Reassemble
steps.instruction: Refit the fan assembly (reconnect plug, expansion line, T25, new zip tie for wiring), airbox/ducting and intake snorkel; reconnect the MAF sensor.
warnings: Torque values for these fasteners not sourced; snug only.

steps.title: Verify
steps.instruction: Start the engine, let it run briefly, shut off and recheck belt alignment on all pulleys; then run again and check noise and charging.
warnings: If the belt walks off or squeals, stop and re-inspect pulleys/tensioner.

safety: Engine cold, key out; keep hands and hair clear of belt, fans and pulleys.
Tensioner is under strong spring pressure; release with the correct T60 and long handle and hold it controlled.
Aluminium tensioner bolt is single-use; replace every time it is removed.
Do not publish or rely on the idler pulley torque until conflict resolved.
Torque + angle figures come from secondary sources only; verify with BMW repair data when possible.
Support the car properly if you raise the front.
missingEvidence: BMW-issued repair instruction (ISTA) with torque for tensioner bolt, idler pulley bolt and alternator pulley.
Idler pulley bolt torque (40 Nm vs 80 Nm conflict).
Tensioner lock pin diameter and whether this tensioner uses one.
An official belt routing diagram and belt direction (ETK diagram image not readable as text).
Whether the E14 external Torx size for the tensioner bolt is correct (single source).
Any E90 sedan (not E82/E60/generic) video or photo confirming fan/intake removal order.
ownerInputsNeeded: Photo of the belt path and the old belt's printed part number/length (6PK1990 expected).
Whether the car is manual or automatic (T25 oil-cooler fastener on automatics) and whether it has A/C.
Condition/noise of tensioner and idler pulleys when the belt is off.

visuals.title: N52 accessory drive: which pulleys are on the belt

elements.describe: A single six-rib serpentine belt (6PK1990) driving the accessories.
The spring tensioner with roller pulley that holds the belt tight.
The Torx-type socket point on the tensioner that is turned clockwise with a long ratchet to relieve tension.
The deflection (idler) pulley mounted at the alternator, with a protective cap.
The alternator driven by the belt.
The A/C compressor driven by the same belt.
The power steering pump driven by the same belt.
The crankshaft pulley at the bottom of the belt run.
